original_question: Using the Bott vanishing theorem, Morita showed that the MMM classes κi for surface bundles vanish in H ∗ (Diff(Σg ); R) for i > 2. Do they also vanish in bounded cohomology Hb∗ (Diff(Σg ); R)?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Question 3.3 ('Bott Vanishing theorem in bounded cohomology').
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper's official formulation very closely: it identifies Morita's use of Bott vanishing, the MMM classes κ_i for surface bundles, the ordinary real cohomology group H^*(Diff(Σ_g); R), the range i > 2, and the bounded-cohomology follow-up question. It is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Question 3.3.
missing_details: State the cohomological degree: κ_i is the i-th MMM class and lives in degree 2i.
Specify what Σ_g is: a closed oriented surface of genus g.

Clarify that Diff(Σ_g) is the diffeomorphism group being used for group cohomology, so the intended setting is the discrete-group/classifying-space one rather than continuous cohomology of the topological group.
Say explicitly that the bounded-cohomology question asks for vanishing for every i > 2, degree-by-degree in H_b^{2i}.
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, note that these are the MMM classes associated to flat Σ_g-bundles/classifying maps through Diff(Σ_g) in the group-cohomological sense.
refined_question: Let Σ_g be a closed oriented surface of genus g, and let κ_i ∈ H^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) denote the i-th Miller-Morita-Mumford class for flat Σ_g-bundles, where Diff(Σ_g) is viewed as a discrete group for group cohomology. Morita showed, using the Bott vanishing theorem, that κ_i = 0 in H^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) for every i > 2. Does the same vanishing hold in bounded group cohomology; that is, is κ_i = 0 in H_b^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) for every i > 2?
justification: The paper introduces Section 3 as a bounded-cohomology section and then, in Section 3.2, asks exactly this question under the heading 'Bott Vanishing theorem in bounded cohomology': first in the broader form 'Do we have the Bott vanishing theorem in bounded cohomology? More concretely,' and then as Question 3.3 about the MMM classes κ_i and the range i > 2. The introduction supplies only broad thematic context about group cohomology and boundedness properties, not a narrower reformulation or an equivalent proposition/theorem nearby, so the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is to keep Question 3.3 itself and only unpack the notation needed to make it stand-alone.
